title: Bond Question 1: Senior Citizen Facility Improvement, Construction and Equipment

context.text: Authorized for the ballot by the New Mexico Legislature under the 2026 Capital Projects General Obligation Bond Act. No bonds are issued unless a majority of voters approve; each bond question is voted on separately.
HB 248, which placed the three bond questions on the ballot, passed the House 65-0 and the Senate 38-0 and was signed by Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham on March 10, 2026, according to Ballotpedia News.

question.text: The 2026 Capital Projects General Obligation Bond Act authorizes the issuance and sale of senior citizen facility improvement, construction and equipment acquisition bonds. Shall the state be authorized to issue general obligation bonds in an amount not to exceed twenty-one million five hundred eighty-two thousand two hundred thirteen dollars ($21,582,213) to make capital expenditures for certain senior citizen facility improvement, construction and equipment acquisition projects and provide for a general property tax imposition and levy for the payment of principal of, interest on and expenses incurred in connection with the issuance of the bonds and the collection of the tax as permitted by law?

summary.text: Asks voters to authorize the state to issue general obligation bonds not to exceed $21,582,213 for senior citizen facility improvement, construction and equipment acquisition projects. Repayment of principal and interest is by a statewide property tax levy. The guide says the State Board of Finance will set the final rate and estimated cost after the election, with bonds generally issued with maturities up to eleven years, and that the amount of property tax collected depends on existing and new debt service, assessed valuation, interest rates and timing.

measure.yesMeans: Authorizes the state to issue general obligation bonds up to $21,582,213 for senior citizen facility improvement, construction and equipment acquisition projects, paid for through a statewide property tax.
measure.noMeans: Does not authorize these bonds; the projects would not be funded by this bond issue.

fiscalImpact.text: The Secretary of State's voter guide (final ballot amounts) says the three bond questions total $393,131,780 including issuance costs ($21,582,213, $19,324,188 and $352,225,379). Separately, the Legislative Finance Committee's February 2026 report on the House Taxation and Revenue Committee substitute for HB 248 (an earlier version totaling about $392.5 million, so its figures differ slightly from the final amounts) said general obligation bond capacity of about 0.136 percent of net taxable property value means that authorizing no more than that capacity maintains a flat mill levy. The guide says the State Board of Finance will determine the final property tax rate and estimated annual cost after the election.

researchNotes: Source: the New Mexico Secretary of State's 2026 Voter Guide and ballot question text. The guide publishes no arguments for or against the bond questions and no statement of a per-household tax cost, so none are included. Ballotpedia's dollar amounts for the bond questions ($30 million, $20 million and $230 million) differ from the official ballot text used here. The fiscal report cited is for the committee substitute of HB 248 and its dollar figures (about $392.5 million total) differ slightly from the final ballot amounts. No campaign committees or named supporters/opponents and no published arguments were found for this bond question.
